 Wait, isn’t Florida’s rainy season over? 
 By Ric Kearbey Published : Nov. 19, 2026 at 5:01 PM EST | Updated : 5 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SARASOTA, Fla. (WWSB) - Wait a minute! Isn’t Florida’s rainy season over?
 Then what’s with these showers and thunderstorms in the forecast?
 Well, here’s the thing.
 Florida’s rainy season typically winds down in October, but that doesn’t mean somebody turns off the rain!
 During summer, our afternoon thunderstorms are fueled by intense sunshine, abundant moisture and daily sea breezes.
 But November plays by a different set of rules.
 Now, cold fronts, upper-level disturbances and changing wind patterns become more important, just like we’re seeing this week.
 And this winter, our normally dry season could get a serious boost from a likely very strong El Niño!
 You’ve heard of El Niño. Those unusually warm waters near the equator in the Pacific Ocean.
 The biggest impact for us? A more active southern jet stream, typically sending additional storm systems across Florida throughout the winter. It could even cause an increased chance of strong to severe storms. 
 So yes, Florida’s rainy season is over.
 But El Niño may have other plans for our winter.
